description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Properties and its Applications".

questions.question: What is the correct way to implement a read-only property 'Add' in a class?
questions.explanation: A read-only property is defined by providing only a 'get' accessor. Option C is a read-write property, and Option B fails because 'ad' is not declared.

questions.question: What is the correct way to implement a write-only property 'Add' in a class?
questions.explanation: A write-only property is created by providing only the 'set' accessor. Option A causes infinite recursion by assigning a value to the property itself instead of a backing field.

questions.question: Which statement about C# properties is correct?

options.text: A property can simultaneously be read-only and write-only
A property must always have both get and set accessors
A write-only property only uses the get accessor
A read-only property only uses the get accessor

questions.explanation: Properties provide a flexible mechanism to read, write, or compute the values of private fields. Read-only properties lack a 'set' block.
